title: Harden SSE framing: recover from trailing-delimiter slips and out-of-order events
author: Maya Singh
release_notes: Fixes intermittent SSE stream corruption where repeated or slipped delimiters could cause partial JSON to be emitted and tool/function-call ordering to appear scrambled. Adds recovery heuristics and observability metrics; toggled behind SSE_STRICT for compatibility.
description: Context: We observed a class of production incidents where clients received malformed or out-of-order SSE events during high-concurrency bursts. Root cause analysis for SUP-1287 showed two correlated behaviors: (1) 'trailing-delimiter slips' -- repeated CRLF/\n delimiters (sometimes from proxy buffering) would create an empty event emission or cause the parser to prematurely flush a partially-received JSON object; and (2) status/heartbeat events injected by intermediaries could interleave with function-call sentinel tokens, producing sequences where a function call start/stop was split across events and reassembled in the wrong order. Motivation: fix these without changing the external stream semantics or breaking existing clients. Goals: (a) make the SSE parser tolerant and recover partial JSON safely when boundaries are noisy, (b) preserve token-level order for function/tool call sentinels unless a real gap exists, and (c) add metrics and a deterministic test harness to prevent regressions. Implementation summary: - Introduce a "delimiter-slip detector" in serve/sse/parser.go that treats repeated adjacent delimiters as potential boundary noise. Instead of emitting an empty event, the parser accumulates consecutive delimiter-adjacent fragments into a short reassembly buffer and attempts to emit only when a syntactically complete JSON/line is detected. The detector looks for balanced braces and string-termination heuristics to avoid waiting indefinitely. - Add an out-of-order tolerant event queue keyed by event sequence id (when provided) and arrival timestamp. The queue holds short windows (configurable default max_reorder_ms=150) to allow slightly late fragments to be reordered before delivery. If the window expires, we emit with instrumentation marking a reorder_exceeded. - Ensure openai-compat streaming_adapter preserves function-call sentinel atomicity by gating function-call emission until both the sentinel and its JSON payload pass the completeness checks. This prevents partial function-call payloads from surfacing when delimiters slip. - New observability metrics: sse.parser.delimiter_slips (count), sse.parser.recovered_events (count), sse.parser.reorder_window_exceeded (count), and sse.parser.reassembly_latency_ms (histogram). Metrics are exposed to the existing metrics registry. - Tests: property-based randomized fragment generator and a deterministic replay case (ci/harness/replay-cases/replay_SUP-1287.yaml) that replays the incident observed in production. parser_test.go includes aggressive fuzz cases with injected duplicate delimiters, interleaved heartbeats, and byte-level splits across UTF-8 multi-byte characters. - Backwards compatibility: behavior is behind a runtime toggle SSE_STRICT; default is tolerant mode. Documentation updated in docs/streaming-framing.md with migration guidance. Checklist: - [x] Implement delimiter-slip detector and small reassembly buffer - [x] Add reorder-tolerant queue and config knobs - [x] Add metrics and expose in metrics_registry - [x] Add deterministic replay case for SUP-1287 - [x] Update openai-compat adapter to gate function-call emissions - [x] Add unit/integration tests and CI harness - [x] Add docs and migration notes Related: this builds on previous streaming work but is a distinct recovery strategy focused on noisy boundary conditions. No DB or protocol-breaking changes.
